info.title: vast-comfy web API
info.description: Hand-kept contract of apps/web (apps/web/tests/routes.test.ts fails when it and the registered Fastify routes diverge). Identity is a signed session cookie set by GET /auth/callback after an OIDC login at Authentik (authorization code flow with PKCE); every /api route needs it (401 without, 403 for the wrong role or for an account whose groups map to no role). Public routes are exactly /healthz, the static files and /auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/logout. CSRF rule for every POST (/api/* and /auth/logout): an Origin header, when present, must equal the origin of WEB_PUBLIC_URL; a Sec-Fetch-Site header, when present, must be same-origin; without Origin the request needs Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin; otherwise 403 csrf. POSTs need Content-Type application/json (415). /api and /auth responses carry Cache-Control: no-store. Unknown routes are 404; errors are {error: {code, message}}. The static route is listed as /{path}; Fastify registers it as the wildcard /*.

sessionCookie.name: __Host-vc_session
sessionCookie.description: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ session cookie (an HS256-signed token with sub, username, name, email, the role groups, iat and exp; lifetime WEB_SESSION_TTL_H) set by GET /auth/callback. With an http://localhost WEB_PUBLIC_URL (development only) the name is vc_session without Secure; each mode ignores the other name.

start_failure.description: The newest start failed after Start returned (it is cleared by the next Start). A fixed code, its fixed plain text (slow_download names the measured speed, a number only), where the server was and the measured speed.

menu.description: The tool menu of the page, in display order: the profile's categories that have entries, and one entry per built-in tool (plain generate, plain edit, upscale) and per enabled style (a style offered in two modes has one entry per mode). Never templates, node ids, file names or LoRA details. The request shapes of /api/generate, /api/edit and /api/upscale do not change: an entry only tells the page which request to send and which style id to put in it.

prompt_optional.description: True when the style has its own prompt text: the user's prompt is optional notes added to it, and the whole must fit GENERATE_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS

references.description: How many reference images an edit with this style needs (the server refuses another count with code style_reference_count); null means the usual edit rule

defaults.description: Values the page pre-fills when the style is chosen; the user can change each. Only the keys the style sets. The server never applies them on its own: a request runs with what it sends

guidance.description: The guidance (cfg) range for every mode whose workflow maps cfg (see advanced); null when the profile offers none. default is the cfg the workflows ship with: the page sends no cfg while the user leaves it there, so the job runs exactly as without the Advanced section. Effects on this model are unverified

cfg.description: The mode's workflow takes a guidance value (within guidance)

LoginError.description: Values of the login_error query parameter that /auth/login and /auth/callback put on the redirect to /. Never provider text. access_denied: the provider refused, or the account's groups map to no role (no session is issued); state_mismatch: missing, mismatched, expired or replayed login transaction; provider_error: the provider reported an error or could not be reached; exchange_failed: the code exchange failed (also a replayed code); token_invalid: the ID token failed verification; nonce_mismatch; no_subject; session_too_large: the session would not fit in a cookie; failed: anything else.

seq.description: Increases by one per line and keeps counting across a new Start (persisted with the lines)

t.description: Epoch UTC seconds when the web process first saw the line

source.description: vast_status: Vast status_msg (docker pull progress); vast_logs: the container's PID 1 stdout; agent: a summary of the agent's /status

text.description: Masked (known secrets, tskey-*, Bearer, Authorization, *key/token/secret/password values, long hex/base64, URL credentials) and cut to BOOT_LOG_MAX_LINE_CHARS; the instance hostname is shown as [host]. Render as text only

generation.description: Changes when a new Start clears the console; the page then drops its lines (also when last_seq is below the after it sent)

state.description: Registry status of the console's instance (creating, booting, ready, stopping), or none once it ended

ended.description: The instance is gone; the last lines are kept until the next Start

phases.description: Always every phase in this fixed order: image_pull, net_probe, install_tools, failsafe, tailscale, agent, nodes, models, comfyui, ready

lines.description: Lines with seq > after, oldest first (at most BOOT_LOG_MAX_LINES are kept)

truncated.description: Lines after the requested seq were already dropped from the ring

source_error.description: The last Vast read for the console failed; the kept lines are still returned

UsageStopReason.description: Why a session ended. destroy_button: the Destroy button in the web (stop_by names who; also when it was pressed while the create was still uncertain). idle_timeout: the instance agent destroyed it after the idle time. failsafe_deadline: the failsafe deadline passed (standalone failsafe or agent). hard_cap: the hard cap passed (web or instance side). boot_failed: Start failed, the create never appeared, the boot timed out (BOOT_TIMEOUT_MIN), the container never started (VAST_START_STUCK_MIN) or the instance destroyed itself because its boot failed. agent_unreachable: the web destroyed it because the agent stayed unreachable for UNREACHABLE_DESTROY_MIN. gone: the instance disappeared and the cause is unknown (e.g. Vast removed it). When the web itself stops the instance it records the reason before acting; when the instance disappears by itself the reason comes from the last agent status the web saw: the agent's own destroy state and reason first, then the earliest idle, failsafe or hard-cap deadline that had passed by the moment the web noticed (plus USAGE_REASON_SLACK_S), else gone. Extending a deadline is never a stop reason.

vast_instance_id.description: Vast instance id; null when no instance was created (a Start that failed before the create)

gpu_name.description: GPU model of the chosen offer (plain characters only)

dph.description: USD per hour: the offer's price, replaced by Vast's own price for the instance once listed

started_at.description: Epoch seconds when the Start was accepted

ready_at.description: Epoch seconds when the web first saw the instance ready; null if it never was

ended_at.description: Epoch seconds of the end; null while active. When the web stopped the instance itself (or a Start failed): the moment it saw the stop complete. When the instance disappeared by itself: for a passed idle, failsafe or hard-cap deadline the deadline itself; for the agent's own destroy reason, the failsafe's pending destroy or an unknown cause (gone) the last time the web saw the agent (after a web restart the last saved sighting, at most about USAGE_REASON_SLACK_S older); always clamped between that last sighting and the moment the web noticed the instance gone; without any sighting the moment it noticed

duration_s.description: ended_at (or now while active) minus started_at

estimated_cost.description: duration_s x dph in USD: an ESTIMATE (disk and traffic are billed separately, and Vast bills by its own clock). Null without an instance or a price

started_by.description: User name of the admin who pressed Start (never an email address); null when unknown (a session from before the history existed)

reason.description: Why it stopped; null while active

stop_by.description: User name of the admin who pressed Destroy (reason destroy_button only)

active.description: True for the running session (ended_at and reason are null)

location.description: Where the session's server was (Vast's row, else the offer); null for sessions recorded before this field existed

down_mbps.description: Download speed of that server in Mbps

StartFailureCode.description: Fixed code of a start that failed after POST /api/start returned. Every release below needs two consecutive reconciles at least a minute apart (a failed Vast or agent read is no sample) and only ever judges a record that is still booting (never one that reached ready). start_stuck: the container never started (last_started null; exited/stopped, created with a stopped intent or state, or a stopped intent without status) once the instance was older than VAST_START_STUCK_MIN (an image still loading, a running container whose agent is not up yet and 'created' with a running intent are never stuck). boot_stopped: it had started and then stopped during the boot; the machine is not avoided. slow_boot: Vast reports it running but its agent has never answered for BOOT_AGENT_GRACE_MIN, counted from the first reconcile that saw it running (the machine did not finish starting up in time). slow_download: the model download, at the average speed seen over at least MODEL_ETA_MIN_OBSERVE_S, would still take more than BOOT_MAX_DOWNLOAD_ETA_MIN, or would end after BOOT_TIMEOUT_MIN; also shown when the instance's own early network probe gave up (container log marker '[boot] FAILED: slow_network'). boot_failed: the instance disappeared during its boot without the web asking (it gave up by itself); its machine is avoided only when nothing says why or the failure was its own (slow_network, disk_insufficient). The web released or noted it (usage reason boot_failed); for start_stuck, slow_boot and slow_download the next Starts avoid that machine for VAST_BAD_MACHINE_TTL_MIN when its machine id is known.

post.summary: Make a short video (member or admin; shares the generate rate limit). 404 video_unavailable when the profile has no enabled video section. Text to video, or image to video when `image` (exactly one base64 start image, validated like an edit reference: magic bytes, size, pixels, side) is sent. Size and duration are names from video in /api/state. Poll the returned id with GET /api/generate/{id} (a video job times out after VIDEO_TIMEOUT_S, not GENERATE_TIMEOUT_S); when done its file is listed under `videos` and served by GET /api/video/{id}/{index}. The job's label is "Video: <size>, <duration>" plus ", from an image". A video cannot be saved to the gallery (phase 1). With `family` (video_families in /api/state) that family's workflow for the mode is used and its title joins the label: "Video: <size>, <duration>, <family title>".

family.description: A family id from video_families in /api/state; absent or the base id: the video section. A family's text mode (no image) and image mode (one start image) have their own workflows; its sizes and durations are its own. Refused with 400 unknown_family for an id this server does not offer, 409 video_models_not_ready while the instance lacks the family's files or reports only some of the mode's experts linked

post.summary: Download the video model files onto the running instance (admin). The agent checks that the instance serves, that ComfyUI has the video node classes and that the disk holds the files, then downloads only the missing files in the background (single-flight; a second call changes nothing). Image jobs keep running; the download counts as activity for the idle shutdown. Progress: video.models in /api/state. With `url`, that file replaces the diffusion model (NOT integrity-pinned or licence-checked; a .gguf file needs the GGUF loader node and is loaded with it). Text encoder and VAE stay pinned. With `family`, that video family's files (single-flight across families: another running download is refused with 409 video_download_busy); its progress is video_families[].models in /api/state. GGUF support of the 14B experts is UNVERIFIED.

url.description: Optional model link (same rules as video_model_url of /api/start); absent, null or blank: the pinned diffusion model (an active link is dropped)

family.description: A video family id (video_families in /api/state) other than the base one: downloads that family's missing files. Absent, null or the base id: the video section (with `url`)

mode.description: text or image: the mode whose experts `links` replace (needed with links)

links.description: Only with a family: one link per expert slot of `mode` (slots in video_families), all of them together or none (one-sided is refused with invalid_model_link; two links to one file name with model_link_name_clash). Each is checked like video_model_url and again on the instance; NOT integrity-pinned. The other mode's links are kept; a family download without links returns the whole family to its pinned files

reason.description: Why a download failed (scrubbed agent text)

models.description: The video model files on the running instance: ready after a boot with Include video models or a finished on-demand download; null without an instance or when its agent does not say
